channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD rises above $58.00 on renewed US-Iran peace talks
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) rises after registering modest gains in the previous day, trading around $58.20 per troy ounce during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: More pain likely if fails to hold $77
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), futures on NYMEX, holds onto early losses, trading 7.6% lower at around $78.60 during the Asian trading session on Monday.

item.title: United States Dollar Index weakens below 100.00 as Trump says new Iran talks would begin Monday
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), an index of the value of the US Dollar (USD) measured against a basket of six world currencies, currently trades near 99.70 in the Asian trading hours on Monday. The DXY declines amid improved risk sentiment.

item.title: Canadian Dollar drifts lower as falling oil prices counter weak USD amid Iran hopes
item.description: The USD/CAD pair kicks off the new week on a positive note, though it lacks bullish conviction and remains confined within Friday's broader range. Spot prices currently trade around the 1.4030 region, up less than 0.10% for the day amid mixed fundamental cues.

item.title: Japan's Katayama says no comment on whether there was FX intervention on Monday
item.description: Japan's Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Monday that she has no comment on whether there was foreign exchange (FX) intervention today, Reuters reported.

item.title: Australian Dollar remains stronger following China’s RatingDog Manufacturing PMI data
item.description: AUD/USD depreciates after opening at a bullish gap, remaining in the positive territory and trading around 0.7030 during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: New Zealand holds gains near 0.5900 despite weaker China PMI data
item.description: The NZD/USD pair holds positive ground near 0.5890 during the Asian trading hours on Monday. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) remains firm despite the downbeat Chinese economic data.

item.title: Australian Dollar languishes near April low as joint US-Japan intervention lifts Yen
item.description: The AUD/JPY cross turns lower for the fifth straight day after a modest uptick to the 111.20 region on Monday and drops to its lowest level since early April during the Asian session.

item.title: British Pound struggles despite easing risk aversion
item.description: GBP/USD holds losses after three days of gains, trading around 1.3470 during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: China’s RatingDog Manufacturing PMI declines to 50.9 in July
item.description: China's RatingDog Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) eased to 50.9 in July from 51.7 in June the latest data published by RatingDog showed on Monday. The market forecast was for a 51.5 reading.

item.title: US President Donald Trump says Iran talks to begin Monday after canceling attack
item.description: US President Donald Trump said that fresh round of Iran talks would begin Monday after he cancelled a planned attack on Iran partially in response to pleas from US allies in the Middle East, including Saudi Arabia, Bloomberg reported on Monday.

item.title: Euro holds near mid-1.1500s, highest level since June 17 as receding Fed hike bets hit USD
item.description: The EUR/USD pair builds on last week's breakout momentum above the 1.1460-1.1470 horizontal barrier and attracts buyers for the fifth straight day on Monday.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7898 vs. 6.7894 previous
item.description: On Monday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.7898 compared to Friday's fix of 6.7894.

item.title: Gold recovers above $4,050 as Trump pauses Iran strikes
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) attracts some buyers to around $4,060 during the early Asian session on Monday. The precious metal edges higher amid hopes of a breakthrough between the United States (US) and Iran after reports that US President Donald Trump has held off Iran strikes.

item.title: Breaking: Japanese Yen rises above 155.50 as Japan announces joint intervention with the US
item.description: The USD/JPY pair tumbles to near 155.45, the lowest since May 6, during the early Asian trading hours on Monday. The Japanese Yen (JPY) attracts some buyers following reports of more joint intervention by the United States (US) and Japan.

item.title: Japan’s Mimura: Joint intervention could mark peak of US-Japan currency partnership
item.description: Atsushi Mimura, Japan’s Vice Finance Minister for International Affairs and top foreign exchange official, said that joint intervention could mark the peak of US-Japan currency partnership, Reuters reported on Monday.

item.title: WTI holds losses near $79.00 amid Middle East peace talks, OPEC+ output expansion
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude oil price gains ground after opening with a bearish gap, remaining nearly 7% down to trade around $79.30 per barrel during Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: Japanese Yen softens, traders watch further US-Japan joint currency intervention
item.description: The USD/JPY pair recovers some lost ground to near 157.65, snapping the three-day losing streak during the early Asian trading hours on Monday.

item.title: OPEC+ agrees to boost September production by 188,000 barrels per day
item.description: The Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies (OPEC+) agreed on Sunday to boost oil production by 188,000 barrels a day (bpd) from September, against a backdrop of disruption caused by the Mideast war.

item.title: Australian Dollar gathers strength to near 0.7050 as Trump cancels Iran strikes
item.description: The AUD/USD pair gains ground to near 0.7040 during the early Asian session on Monday. The Australian Dollar (AUD) strengthens against the US Dollar (USD) on improved risk sentiment after the reports that US President Donald Trump holds off Iran strikes.

item.title: Middle East War updates: Trump holds off Iran strikes on pledge Hormuz deal is close
item.description: Here’s a brief recap of the key developments in the Middle East war that occurred over the weekend, which are expected to have a significant impact on markets in the upcoming week.

item.title: US and Israel plan to attack Iran's energy infrastructure – CBS News
item.description: CBS News reported that the United States and Israel may engage in a large campaign against Iran, targeting Iran's energy infrastructure, said multiple sources.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Bulls eye 0.6000 after SMA break
item.description: The Kiwi Dollar extends its three-day rally, climbing above 0.5850 and is poised to challenge 0.5900 amid improving risk appetite and broad US Dollar weakness. The clearance of the 200-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) supports the bullish trend, as traders eye the May monthly high at 0.5995.

item.title: Forecasting the upcoming week: US labor market takes center stage after hawkish Fed split
item.description: The first full week of August will test whether the US Dollar can recover from its sell-off during the last week of July as investors shift their attention from central bank decisions to a fresh round of economic data.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Bulls defend 50-day SMA as rebound builds
item.description: The USD/CHF bounces off weekly lows and meanders around 0.8080 after hitting a daily high of 0.8127, amid presumed intervention, with Nikkei reporting that the US Treasury Department has told currency market participants to prepare for additional intervention, following Thursday's action by Japanese

item.title: Gold slides as US yields surge, keeping $4,100 out of reach
item.description: Gold price tumbles nearly 1.50% on Friday as the US Dollar recovers some ground after Japanese authorities intervened in the foreign exchange markets a day ago, driving the Greenback to a 30-day low before recovering, according to the US Dollar Index (DXY). The XAU/USD trades at $4,045.

item.title: The Japanese Yen has a second buyer nobody will name
item.description: Thursday's record Yen defence is the story everyone has written.

item.title: United States Dollar Index struggles near 100 after suspected Japanese intervention
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) struggles to hold its early recovery on Friday as the fallout from suspected Japanese intervention and the possibility of direct action by the United States (US) keep the Greenback under pressure.

item.title: Fed's Barkin: It's a close call whether interest rates are high enough
item.description: Richmond Federal Reserve (Fed) President Tom Barkin said on Friday that it remains uncertain whether the current level of interest rates is sufficiently restrictive to bring inflation back to the Fed's 2% target, according to an interview with The Wall Street Journal.

item.title: Euro recovers as Eurozone inflation stays firm
item.description: EUR/USD trades near the 1.1530 area during Friday's American session, consolidating after a strong rally off intraday lows. The Euro found support from resilient Eurozone inflation data, although gains remain capped as hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) rhetoric boosts the US Dollar.
